title: Section 3
context: Two university students, Maya and Tom, are discussing their research project on students' social media habits.

audio.t: You will hear two students, Maya and Tom, discussing a research project about social media habits.
Hi Tom. Have you thought any more about our project for the research methods course?
Yes, I have. I was going to suggest something about sleep, because I read that late-night phone use affects how well students concentrate.
That's interesting, but my idea was more about social media itself. My flatmate says she can't study for twenty minutes without checking her phone.
Hmm, that does sound more original. And the tutor did say she wanted topics close to our own experience.
Exactly. So we'd look at how undergraduates actually use social media, and perhaps touch on sleep as one factor.
Fine by me. Now, how are we going to collect the data? I think face-to-face interviews would give us richer answers.
They would, but we only have six weeks, and transcribing every interview takes forever.
True. So an online questionnaire, then. We can send the link round the student groups.
Right. And how many people should we aim for? I was thinking two hundred.
Dr Kowalski told me that was far too many for a project this size, because we'd never have time to analyse them all.
Oh, I didn't know that. Did she suggest a number?
She said eighty would be too small to show any pattern, and a hundred and twenty would be about right.
A hundred and twenty it is, then.
My worry about questionnaires is that people don't tell the truth about how long they spend online.
That's a good point. They nearly always underestimate it.
So instead of just asking, we could ask them to send a screenshot of the screen-time report on their phones.
That's much more reliable. I'll add that to the questionnaire.
Have you looked at the ethics form yet? I couldn't tell what's the most difficult part.
I thought the consent section would be the hard bit, but it's actually quite simple, just a tick box.
The tricky part is that we have to promise participants' names will never be linked to their screenshots, so we have to delete the names straight away.
Okay, so anonymity is the main issue. I can take care of that bit.
Thanks. Now, before we start, we ran a small pilot with ten friends last week. Shall we go through what it showed?
Sure. What about Instagram? I expected it to be popular with everyone.
Not with the first-years, actually. Most of them said they use it less than they did last year.
Interesting. And TikTok? I guessed it would be the one that people use after midnight.
That's what I thought too, but no. It was the platform where people spent the longest each day, around two and a half hours.
Wow. Then which one was the late-night one?
YouTube. Most of them said they watch it in bed, usually after twelve.
That makes sense. What about WhatsApp?
Almost everyone said they use it for study groups, to share notes and organise meetings.
And Facebook? I remember a couple of people mentioning it for the news.
Only for one person. In general, hardly any of our participants used it at all.
Right. So that's something we should highlight in our report.
Agreed. Shall we draft the questionnaire together this afternoon?
Yes, let's meet in the library at two.

options: Her flatmate's habits gave her the idea.
She had read an article about it.

questions.explain: Maya định 200, nhưng Tiến sĩ Kowalski nói quá nhiều; 80 thì quá ít, "a hundred and twenty would be about right".

by reducing the length of the questionnaire

blocks.instructions: What did the pilot study show about each social media platform? Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A-G, next to Questions 6-10.
options: A  used mainly for group study
C  the most daily time per user
G  used more by men than by women

questions.explain: "Not with the first-years ... they use it less than they did last year" nghĩa là giảm ở sinh viên năm nhất.
Tom đoán dùng sau nửa đêm nhưng Maya sửa: đây là nền tảng "where people spent the longest each day".
Nền tảng dùng khuya là YouTube: "they watch it in bed, usually after twelve".
"Almost everyone said they use it for study groups".
Chỉ một người dùng cho tin tức, còn nhìn chung "hardly any of our participants used it at all".
